chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan and Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever makes the Hereafter his greatest concern every morning and evening, Allah will make contentment in his heart, gather his affairs for him, and he will not leave this world until his sustenance is completed. And whoever makes the world his greatest concern every morning and evening, Allah will put poverty between his eyes, scatter his affairs, and he will not attain from the world except what was ordained for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between making the Hereafter or the world your main concern?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith highlights the spiritual mechanics of *Qana'ah* (contentment) as a divine gift for those who anchor their morning and evening intentions in the Hereafter, contrasting it with the fragmentation of affairs (*shatta 'alayhi amruhu*) caused by worldly obsession. This reflects the Shia emphasis on intention (*niyyah*) as the determinant of one's spiritual state, ensuring that sustenance is completed without the anxiety of scarcity. The narration serves as a practical guide for balancing worldly duties with otherworldly focus, a core theme in Twelver Shi'ite ethics.
